lines.text: Almanak decides. KeeperHub lands it. And the strategy code never changes.
Every DeFi agent framework has the same blind spot. The strategy is the interesting part. Execution is where it actually breaks.
Almanak compiles a strategy down to raw calldata, then hands it to an executor that has to sign it, broadcast it, survive a stuck nonce, and never, ever send it twice.
Almanak's execution layer is three abstract classes. A Signer, a Submitter, and a Simulator.
So I implemented all three against KeeperHub. The strategy has no idea. The only change to Almanak's own demo strategy is a single line, adding Base Sepolia to its supported chains.
Now every transaction the strategy plans goes through KeeperHub's enclave wallet, its spending caps, its simulation, and its audit log. Gas is sponsored. The private key never touches my process.
Here it is running on Base Sepolia. A real strategy tick, a real approve, a real deposit, verified on chain.
The strategy plans an approve and a deposit. Both are dry-run through KeeperHub first, then broadcast through it.
Both land. Both come back verified, with KeeperHub's relayer paying the gas, so the organization wallet never needs a native balance.
The same run is visible in the local console, in the KeeperHub dashboard, and from a Telegram bot on my phone.
But an execution backend is judged on what it does when things go wrong. So I built six failure modes and recorded every one.
An unknown selector is refused before anything is signed. A call that would revert is caught by the dry run. A duplicate is blocked by an idempotency key bound to the intent, not to the attempt.
And when the process is killed in the middle of a bundle, it resumes from the receipts log, and never broadcasts the same transaction twice.
Twenty out of twenty unsafe calls refused. Ten out of ten dry runs caught. Five out of five transactions landed, median six point nine seconds.
A hundred and thirty unit tests. And three issues I filed against KeeperHub itself, all three accepted by the maintainers, all three now open as pull requests.
Almanak strategies, executed by KeeperHub. No strategy code changes.
